title: Generate an image from a prompt (and edit an existing image)
contract: `image_generate` is one model-callable tool covering text-to-image and image-to-image editing; the router is simply the presence of `image_url`/`reference_image_urls` (media.tool-image-generate). Eight backends resolve behind it — FAL (a 21-model in-tree catalog driving payload construction, size translation and edit routing), OpenAI gpt-image-2 at three quality tiers, OpenAI-via-Codex-OAuth, Krea 2, OpenRouter's Dedicated Image API (up to 16 reference images), xAI Grok Imagine, DeepInfra (live-discovered catalog) and a managed Nous FAL gateway that bills a subscription instead of a personal key. A Clarity Upscaler chain gives a ~2x pass; provider resolution prints an actionable 'no backend' setup message rather than a bare error; `hermes tools` has an Image/Video Generation picker; `fal_common.py` keeps the SDK out of cold start.
governance: Privileged — spends money and writes files. Today `media_gen._queue_cloud` calls the plain `q.enqueue` (agents/core/media_gen.py:132) with risk_tier=2, and `media.image`/`media.video` are **absent** from agents/core/kernel/registry.py, whose media entries are only `media.present` and `media.restore` (registry.py:78,81). So a wired cloud generation would be approval-queued but never kernel-mediated. Must cross a new kernel kind `media.generate` (external/money tier) via `enqueue_mediated` (agents/core/autonomy/queue.py:1031), plus `file.write` for the artifact and `plugin.egress` for the provider call.

title: Register a third-party media backend without touching core
contract: Every media subsystem is a registry lookup with no per-vendor conditionals: `BrowserProvider` (5 abstract methods, scope-aware registry with a generation counter used as a cache fingerprint, `get_setup_schema()` returning None to hide a provider from the picker), `VideoGenProvider`, `TranscriptionProvider`, `register_tts_provider`, `WebSearchProvider`, `TerminalEnvironmentProvider`. Shell-command providers (`tts.providers.<name>`, `stt.providers.<name>`) let any local CLI become a backend with zero Python. `hermes tools post-setup KEY` runs a backend's declared install hook non-interactively.
governance: Read-only in itself (registration and availability probes must be cheap and must never make network calls, per Hermes's own hard rule). Every provider *call* it dispatches crosses `plugin.egress` for a remote backend, or `file.write` for a local one.

title: Look at an image and answer questions about it, mid-conversation
contract: `vision_analyze` is model-callable and framed as an instruction — 'call it any time the user references an image' (media.tool-vision-analyze). It takes a URL, a local path or a data: URL plus a question, and an optional `region` crop in **original-image pixel coordinates applied before any downscaling**, so the documented workflow is 'load the full image, then re-call with a region to zoom into small text'. Two execution paths: a native fast path attaching the image directly to the main model when the provider+model can carry media in a tool result, and an auxiliary-vision path that returns text otherwise (media.computer-use-vision-routing, media.vision-tool-result-support). `agent.image_input_mode` decides how user-attached images on the current turn reach the model, and inline image references are extracted from prose so they attach automatically.
governance: Read-only against a loopback VLM. A cloud vision model crosses `plugin.egress`; keep the screen-reflex hard refusal for non-loopback as the model for any capture-derived image. Registration goes through agents/core/tool_rpc.py, whose kind prefix already routes tool calls through the kernel (`tool.rpc`, registry.py:55).

title: Accept an image safely before it enters conversation history
contract: A layered ingest guard: SSRF checks, size caps and decode validation refuse unsafe/oversized/undecodable images *before* they reach immutable history (media.vision-ingest-guards); normalisation rasterises SVG and coerces to one of the four media types the major vision providers accept (media.vision-normalize); MIME sniffing decides the declared media_type from the bytes and transcodes to PNG when the real type is not universally supported (media.image-mime-transcode); embeds are downscaled proactively and again reactively after a provider size rejection (media.vision-sizing); a CPU-burst semaphore stops an 'analyze every frame' fan-out from starving the event loop (media.vision-cpu-cap); and under a non-local terminal backend, path-like source images reach the provider as data: URLs so a container path never leaks to a third party (media.image-source-confinement). `tools/image_source.py` is the one resolver every path shares.
governance: Read-only, but it is the boundary that decides what enters immutable history and the audit log, so it is security-load-bearing. A remote fetch crosses `plugin.egress`.
remaining_verbatim:
- SVG rasterisation and coercion of other formats to a provider-accepted type (today they are refused)
- MIME sniffing that corrects the declared type and transcodes to PNG instead of rejecting
- Reactive shrink-and-retry after a provider size rejection (the retry scope only retries empty replies)
- A CPU/concurrency cap on image decode/encode fan-out
- One shared image-source resolver used by every image path (composer, camera, tools)

title: Transcribe a voice message or dictated speech
contract: `transcribe_audio` validates, preprocesses and dispatches to the active backend, returning `{success, transcript, provider, error?}` (media.stt-pipeline). Eight backends — local faster-whisper (CPU default, GPU when available), a `local_command` env-var escape hatch, Groq, OpenAI, Mistral Voxtral (13 languages, diarization, word timestamps), xAI, ElevenLabs Scribe (audio-event tagging), DeepInfra — plus shell-command providers, a `TranscriptionProvider` ABC, strict explicit selection with auto-detect only on a never-configured install, a whisper prompt-length cap, cloud silence trimming to cut upload bytes, a picker and `POST /api/audio/transcribe`.
governance: Local transcription is read-only. Any cloud STT crosses `plugin.egress` and ships the owner's recorded speech off-box — the same disclosure class as cloud TTS, and it should be classified rather than a config default.
remaining_verbatim: Un singur backend. Hermes are opt (faster-whisper local, `local_command`, Groq, OpenAI, Mistral Voxtral cu diarizare și timestamp-uri pe cuvânt, xAI, ElevenLabs Scribe, DeepInfra) plus provideri pe comandă de shell, un ABC `TranscriptionProvider`, selecție explicită strictă cu auto-detect doar la o instalare neconfigurată vreodată, un plafon pe lungimea promptului Whisper, trunchierea liniștii înainte de upload ca să scadă octeții trimiși, un picker și `POST /api/audio/transcribe`. Nimic din astea nu e livrat. title: Hold a hands-free voice conversation
contract: Voice mode records the mic, transcribes with the configured STT backend, submits the result as your message and optionally speaks the reply (media.voice-mode). Around it: a push-to-talk key binding normalised so the same config string works in both CLI front ends; audio cues (start/stop tones and an ambient thinking blip); stop phrases that end the conversation when spoken alone; silence-based auto-stop; audio-environment detection that works out whether the host can record at all (PortAudio, PulseAudio, Termux) and prints a platform-correct fix; and `voice_client_config.py` publishing the record key, direct-capture flag, beeps and thresholds so client and backend agree without duplicating config parsing. Server side: `GET /api/audio/voice-config`, `POST /api/audio/speak` + a speak-stream WebSocket, and an ElevenLabs voice list for settings.
governance: Read-only capture. The critical property is the existing one: a voice-initiated turn carries inbound taint, so anything above read-only lands in the decision inbox rather than executing. That must survive every ergonomics change here — a stop phrase or VAD must never become a path that submits a turn with a different origin classification.

title: Wake the assistant hands-free with a spoken phrase
contract: 'Hey Hermes' is an always-on, fully on-device hotword listener that opens a fresh session and captures voice through the existing pipeline — no audio leaves the machine for detection (media.wake-word). Three engines: openWakeWord with the bundled 'hey hermes' ONNX/TFLite model shipped in-tree so it works out of the box; sherpa-onnx keyword spotting that detects **any typed phrase with no training** via a streaming zipformer; and Picovoice Porcupine for built-in keywords and custom .ppn files. Capture mode chooses whether PCM comes from PortAudio on the backend host or is streamed as int16 frames from the desktop/TUI client via `wake.feed`, and profile routing lets different profiles enroll different phrases.
governance: Read-only and, critically, must stay fully on-device — detection audio never leaves the machine, matching the screen-reflex loopback rule. A wake-triggered session inherits the same inbound taint as any voice turn.

title: Search the web and pull clean page content
contract: `web_search` and `web_extract` are two model-callable tools over independently-selectable backends. Eight in-tree providers behind one `WebSearchProvider` ABC — Firecrawl, Parallel.ai, Exa, SearXNG, Brave free tier, DDGS, Keenable, xAI. Resolution walks a legacy preference list, falls back to a keyless MCP ring that round-robins anonymous free tiers so a fresh install can search before configuring anything, and performs an automatic 'rescue' retry when the configured provider fails. A TTL result cache stops repeat lookups re-billing the provider; website policy and URL-safety guards block private/internal addresses and operator-disallowed sites, classifying a policy block separately from a provider failure so the rescue path never retries a deliberate refusal.
